scope: V1 Automatic Prefix Caching hash inputs, block lifecycle, hash granularity, hybrid Mamba checkpoints, metrics and cache isolation.

claims.claim: A V1 prefix block hash includes its parent block hash, current block token IDs and extra hash keys.
claims.notes: Later block identity depends on the preceding token prefix, not just local block contents.

claims.claim: Current request hash extras can include LoRA identity, multimodal feature hashes, cache_salt and prompt-embedding digests.
claims.notes: Different adapters or multimodal inputs must not reuse the same KV state.

claims.claim: Current CacheConfig defaults prefix caching to SHA-256 and documents CBOR-based reproducible variants and non-cryptographic xxHash variants.
claims.notes: The source warns non-cryptographic collision risk can affect correctness and multi-tenant privacy.

claims.claim: V1 BlockPool maps hashes to physical blocks and manages a free-block queue; referenced blocks are protected from eviction and cached blocks can be evicted from the LRU end.
claims.notes: The cache is bounded and is not permanent storage.

claims.claim: When all request tokens appear cached, V1 still recomputes the last token to obtain logits; block alignment can cause the final block to be recomputed.
claims.notes: Implementation detail may change across releases.

claims.claim: Current V1 resolves hash block size to scheduler block size for a single KV group and rejects a different prefix_match_unit while block hashing is active.
claims.notes: For multiple groups the default can be the GCD of prefix-cacheable group block sizes, or an explicit valid prefix_match_unit.

claims.claim: Fine-grained sub-block prefix reuse is a constrained hybrid Mamba path requiring aligned prefix-cacheable groups and shared-prefix checkpoint configuration; it is not a universal arbitrary-token hit guarantee.
claims.notes: Current source implements partial cache entries as lookup metadata associated with an existing physical block; model and alignment conditions apply.

claims.claim: cache_salt is mixed into the first block hash so only requests with the same salt can share the corresponding prefix cache, mitigating timing-based cross-tenant inference.
claims.notes: cache_salt does not replace API authentication, authorization or network isolation.

claims.claim: Automatic Prefix Caching reduces repeated query Prefill work but does not reduce Decode work required to generate new output tokens.
claims.notes: Benefit depends on exact repeated prefixes, cache residency, routing and prompt/output length distribution.
